solution.concept_anchor: GHI publisher — not a UN body
solution.strong_distractor: c — Option c is deceptive because the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is the most prominent UN body associated with hunger data, making students conflate it with the GHI publisher.
elimination_logic: Eliminate option a: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report, not hunger assessments.
Eliminate option c: FAO publishes the State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World report — a separate product entirely.
Eliminate option d: WFP is a UN operational agency focused on food delivery, not index publication.
Retain option b: Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe are the joint publishers of the Global Hunger Index.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The most common trap here is attributing the GHI to a UN body — particularly FAO or WFP — because hunger is a UN-adjacent concern. Students who have read about FAO's State of Food Security report assume GHI is a UN product. The GHI is published by two non-governmental organisations: Concern Worldwide (Irish) and Welthungerhilfe (German). India has specifically criticised the GHI methodology, including its reliance on opinion-poll-based data for undernourishment, which further confuses students into thinking it is a government or intergovernmental report.
solution.final_explanation:
The Global Hunger Index is published jointly by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe — neither of which is a UN agency. This distinction matters because India's government has repeatedly questioned the GHI's methodology on the grounds that its undernourishment indicator is based on an opinion poll of only 3,000 respondents rather than objective nutritional surveys.

• Option (a) — UNDP: Incorrect. UNDP publishes the Human Development Report and HDI-related indices.
• Option (b) — Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe: Correct. Both are international NGOs — Irish and German respectively.
• Option (c) — FAO: Incorrect. FAO co-publishes the State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World (SOFI) report, which is a separate product with different methodology.
• Option (d) — WFP: Incorrect. WFP is an operational UN agency focused on food delivery and emergency response, not index compilation.

Value Addition:
• GHI uses four indicators: undernourishment (weight 1/3), child wasting (1/6), child stunting (1/6), and child mortality (1/3).
• India objects specifically to the use of Gallup opinion polls for the undernourishment component.
• The SOFI report (FAO/WFP/IFAD/WFP/UNICEF) is the UN's primary food security publication — distinct from GHI.

solution.concept_anchor: GHI publisher — not a UN body
solution.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प c भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) भूख से संबंधित डेटा के साथ सबसे प्रमुख संयुक्त राष्ट्र निकाय है, जिससे छात्र इसे GHI प्रकाशक के साथ भ्रमित कर लेते हैं।
elimination_logic: विकल्प a को हटाएं: UNDP मानव विकास रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करता है, भूख आकलन नहीं।
विकल्प c को हटाएं: FAO 'State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World' रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करता है — जो पूरी तरह से अलग उत्पाद है।
विकल्प d को हटाएं: WFP एक संयुक्त राष्ट्र परिचालन एजेंसी है जो खाद्य वितरण पर केंद्रित है, सूचकांक प्रकाशन पर नहीं।
विकल्प b को रखें: Concern Worldwide और Welthungerhilfe ग्लोबल हंगर इंडेक्स के संयुक्त प्रकाशक हैं।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: यहाँ सबसे आम जाल यह है कि GHI को किसी संयुक्त राष्ट्र निकाय — विशेष रूप से FAO या WFP — से जोड़ दिया जाता है क्योंकि भूख एक संयुक्त राष्ट्र से जुड़ा मुद्दा है। जो छात्र FAO की 'State of Food Security' रिपोर्ट के बारे में पढ़ चुके हैं, वे मान लेते हैं कि GHI भी संयुक्त राष्ट्र का उत्पाद है। GHI दो गैर-सरकारी संगठनों द्वारा प्रकाशित किया जाता है: Concern Worldwide (आयरिश) और Welthungerhilfe (जर्मन)। भारत ने विशेष रूप से GHI की कार्यप्रणाली की आलोचना की है, जिसमें इसके कुपोषण के लिए राय सर्वेक्षण आधारित डेटा का उपयोग शामिल है, जो छात्रों को यह सोचने पर मजबूर करता है कि यह कोई सरकारी या अंतरसरकारी रिपोर्ट है।
solution.final_explanation:
ग्लोबल हंगर इंडेक्स का संयुक्त प्रकाशन Concern Worldwide और Welthungerhilfe द्वारा किया जाता है — जो दोनों संयुक्त राष्ट्र एजेंसियां नहीं हैं। यह भेद महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि भारत सरकार ने बार-बार GHI की कार्यप्रणाली पर सवाल उठाए हैं, विशेषकर इसके कुपोषण संकेतक के लिए जो केवल 3,000 उत्तरदाताओं के राय सर्वेक्षण पर आधारित है, न कि वस्तुनिष्ठ पोषण सर्वेक्षणों पर।

• विकल्प (a) — UNDP: गलत। UNDP मानव विकास रिपोर्ट और HDI संबंधित सूचकांक प्रकाशित करता है।
• विकल्प (b) — Concern Worldwide और Welthungerhilfe: सही। दोनों अंतरराष्ट्रीय गैर-सरकारी संगठन हैं — क्रमशः आयरिश और जर्मन।
• विकल्प (c) — FAO: गलत। FAO 'State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World' (SOFI) रिपोर्ट का सह-प्रकाशक है, जो एक अलग उत्पाद है और इसकी कार्यप्रणाली भिन्न है।
• विकल्प (d) — WFP: गलत। WFP एक परिचालन संयुक्त राष्ट्र एजेंसी है जो खाद्य वितरण और आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया पर केंद्रित है, सूचकांक संकलन पर नहीं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• GHI चार संकेतकों का उपयोग करता है: कुपोषण (भार 1/3), बाल कुपोषण (1/6), बाल वृद्धि रुकावट (1/6), और बाल मृत्यु दर (1/3)।
• भारत विशेष रूप से कुपोषण घटक के लिए Gallup राय सर्वेक्षण के उपयोग का विरोध करता है।
• SOFI रिपोर्ट (FAO/WFP/IFAD/UNICEF) संयुक्त राष्ट्र की प्रमुख खाद्य सुरक्षा प्रकाशन है — जो GHI से भिन्न है।

solution.concept_anchor: HDI income dimension — GNI per capita PPP not GDP

statement_analysis.statement: The standard of living dimension in the Human Development Index is measured using Gross National Income per capita adjusted for purchasing power parity.
statement_analysis.reason: HDI uses GNI per capita (PPP) — not GDP per capita — for the income dimension, reflecting income available to citizens regardless of where it is earned.

statement_analysis.statement: The Gender Development Index and the Gender Inequality Index are published by different UN agencies.
statement_analysis.reason: Both GDI and GII are products of UNDP's Human Development Report — they originate from the same agency and the same flagship report.

statement_analysis.statement: India's rank in the Human Development Index has been constrained despite economic growth partly because of low GNI per capita relative to comparator countries.
statement_analysis.reason: India's HDI rank stagnation is attributed to the drag from GNI per capita (PPP) and education indicators, even as GDP growth rates remain high.

solution.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three correct) is the strongest distractor because statements 1 and 3 are accurate, tempting students to assume statement 2 must also be correct given that both GDI and GII are HDR products.
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: HDI income dimension uses GNI per capita (PPP) — this is correct; GDP is not used.
Test statement 2: Both GDI and GII are UNDP/HDR products, not different agencies — statement 2 is incorrect.
Verify statement 3: GNI per capita and education lags explain India's HDI rank stagnation — correct.
Since statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is incorrect, the answer is option c (1 and 3 only).
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is the key trap. Students often know that GDI and GII measure different things (one measures gender-based development gaps; the other measures gender-based inequality in human development) and incorrectly infer they must come from different publishers. Both indices are UNDP products released through the same Human Development Report. This conflation of 'different metrics' with 'different agencies' is a classic scope-extension trap.
solution.final_explanation:
The HDI framework rests on three dimensions: long and healthy life (measured by life expectancy at birth), knowledge (mean and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (GNI per capita at PPP). The use of GNI rather than GDP is deliberate — GNI captures income of residents regardless of geographic origin of earnings.

• Statement 1 — Correct: GNI per capita (PPP) is the prescribed metric for the income dimension. Using GDP would overstate or understate resident welfare.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Both GDI and GII are published by UNDP as part of the Human Development Report. GDI measures male-female HDI ratio; GII measures inequality in reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation — different metrics, same publisher.
• Statement 3 — Correct: India's HDI rank improvement is tempered by relatively low GNI per capita (PPP) compared to countries with similar growth trajectories, combined with education gaps.

Value Addition:
• HDR is published annually with a specific thematic focus each year (e.g., Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives — 2022).
• GDI is the ratio of female HDI to male HDI; a value of 1 indicates parity.
• India falls in the 'Medium Human Development' category in recent HDR editions.

statement_analysis.statement: मानव विकास सूचकांक में जीवन स्तर आयाम को सकल राष्ट्रीय आय प्रति व्यक्ति को क्रय शक्ति समता के अनुसार समायोजित करके मापा जाता है।
statement_analysis.reason: HDI में आय आयाम के लिए GNI प्रति व्यक्ति (PPP) का उपयोग किया जाता है — GDP प्रति व्यक्ति का नहीं — जो नागरिकों को उपलब्ध आय को दर्शाता है चाहे वह कहीं भी अर्जित की गई हो।

statement_analysis.statement: लिंग विकास सूचकांक और लिंग असमानता सूचकांक अलग-अलग संयुक्त राष्ट्र एजेंसियों द्वारा प्रकाशित किए जाते हैं।
statement_analysis.reason: GDI और GII दोनों UNDP के मानव विकास रिपोर्ट के उत्पाद हैं — ये एक ही एजेंसी और एक ही प्रमुख रिपोर्ट से उत्पन्न होते हैं।

statement_analysis.statement: भारत की मानव विकास सूचकांक में रैंक आर्थिक विकास के बावजूद सीमित रही है, आंशिक रूप से तुलनात्मक देशों की तुलना में कम GNI प्रति व्यक्ति के कारण।
statement_analysis.reason: भारत की HDI रैंक स्थिरता का कारण GNI प्रति व्यक्ति (PPP) और शिक्षा संकेतकों से उत्पन्न बाधा है, जबकि GDP विकास दरें उच्च बनी हुई हैं।

solution.strong_distractor: d — विकल्प d (सभी तीन सही) सबसे मजबूत भ्रमित करने वाला विकल्प है क्योंकि कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं, जिससे छात्र यह मान सकते हैं कि कथन 2 भी सही होगा क्योंकि GDI और GII दोनों HDR के उत्पाद हैं।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 सत्यापित करें: HDI आय आयाम के लिए GNI प्रति व्यक्ति (PPP) का उपयोग होता है — यह सही है; GDP का उपयोग नहीं होता।
कथन 2 का परीक्षण करें: GDI और GII दोनों UNDP/HDR के उत्पाद हैं, अलग एजेंसियां नहीं — कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 3 सत्यापित करें: GNI प्रति व्यक्ति और शिक्षा की कमी भारत की HDI रैंक स्थिरता को समझाती है — सही है।
चूंकि कथन 1 और 3 सही हैं और कथन 2 गलत है, अतः उत्तर विकल्प c (केवल 1 और 3) है।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 मुख्य जाल है। छात्र अक्सर जानते हैं कि GDI और GII अलग-अलग चीजें मापते हैं (एक लिंग आधारित विकास अंतर को मापता है; दूसरा मानव विकास में लिंग आधारित असमानता को मापता है) और गलत तरीके से यह निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि वे अलग-अलग प्रकाशकों से आते होंगे। दोनों सूचकांक UNDP के उत्पाद हैं जो एक ही मानव विकास रिपोर्ट के माध्यम से जारी होते हैं। 'अलग मेट्रिक्स' को 'अलग एजेंसियों' से जोड़ना एक क्लासिक स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन जाल है।
solution.final_explanation:
HDI ढांचा तीन आयामों पर आधारित है: लंबी और स्वस्थ जीवन (जन्म पर जीवन प्रत्याशा द्वारा मापा गया), ज्ञान (औसत और अपेक्षित शिक्षा वर्ष), और जीवन स्तर (GNI प्रति व्यक्ति PPP पर)। GDP के बजाय GNI का उपयोग जानबूझकर किया गया है — GNI आय को दर्शाता है जो निवासियों को प्राप्त होती है चाहे वह आय कहीं भी अर्जित की गई हो।

• कथन 1 — सही: आय आयाम के लिए GNI प्रति व्यक्ति (PPP) निर्धारित मापदंड है। GDP का उपयोग करने से निवासी कल्याण का अतिरंजित या कम आकलन हो सकता है।
• कथन 2 — गलत: GDI और GII दोनों UNDP द्वारा मानव विकास रिपोर्ट के हिस्से के रूप में प्रकाशित होते हैं। GDI पुरुष-स्त्री HDI अनुपात मापता है; GII प्रजनन स्वास्थ्य, सशक्तिकरण, और श्रम बाजार भागीदारी में असमानता मापता है — अलग मेट्रिक्स, एक ही प्रकाशक।
• कथन 3 — सही: भारत की HDI रैंक सुधार तुलनात्मक रूप से कम GNI प्रति व्यक्ति (PPP) और शिक्षा अंतर के कारण सीमित है, जबकि विकास दरें उच्च हैं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• HDR प्रत्येक वर्ष एक विशिष्ट थीम के साथ प्रकाशित होता है (जैसे, Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives — 2022)।
• GDI महिला HDI का पुरुष HDI के अनुपात के रूप में है; 1 का मान समानता दर्शाता है।
• भारत हाल के HDR संस्करणों में 'मध्यम मानव विकास' श्रेणी में आता है।

solution.concept_anchor: GII publisher — WIPO not WEF

statement_analysis.statement: The Global Innovation Index is published by the World Economic Forum in partnership with Cornell University.
statement_analysis.reason: The GII is published by WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization), not WEF, in partnership with INSEAD and Cornell University.

statement_analysis.statement: India's strength in the Global Innovation Index lies specifically in its Innovation Output efficiency relative to its Input sub-index score.
statement_analysis.reason: India's unique distinction in GII is its high output efficiency ratio — meaning it generates proportionally stronger innovation outputs given its input level — a recognised GOI policy talking point.

statement_analysis.statement: The Global Innovation Index evaluates countries across parameters that include Knowledge outputs and Creative outputs as distinct categories.
statement_analysis.reason: GII's seven pillars include Knowledge outputs and Creative outputs as separate sub-indices — these are distinct from the input pillars covering Institutions, Human capital, Infrastructure, Market sophistication, and Business sophistication.

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a (statement 1 only) is the strongest distractor because students who know WEF is a major publisher of competitiveness indices may confidently mark only statement 1 as incorrect, but they must also verify statements 2 and 3.
elimination_logic: Test statement 1: GII is published by WIPO — not WEF. Statement 1 is incorrect.
Test statement 2: India's output efficiency ratio advantage in GII is a documented fact. Statement 2 is correct.
Test statement 3: GII has seven pillars including Knowledge outputs and Creative outputs as distinct categories. Statement 3 is correct.
Only statement 1 is incorrect, so the answer is option a — but since the question asks which are NOT correct, and only one statement qualifies, option a (1 only) is correct.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The WEF-WIPO confusion is a persistent UPSC trap. WEF publishes the Global Competitiveness Index, the Energy Transition Index, and the Global Gender Gap Index — all prominent indices. solution.final_explanation:

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a is the strongest distractor because students who correctly identify both A and R as true may assume the reason automatically explains the assertion without checking the causal link.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? — The Press Freedom Index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), a French NGO. A is correct.
Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — India's government has indeed disputed the subjective methodology of the PFI. R is correct.
Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — India's rebuttal of the methodology does not explain why RSF is the publisher. These are two independent facts about the same index. R does NOT explain A.

solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Students who identify both A and R as factually correct tend to select option a without verifying the causal connection. The Reason describes India's response to the index's findings, which is factually true but has no logical bearing on who publishes the index. The question separates fact-verification from causal reasoning — the hallmark of a well-designed assertion-reason trap.
solution.final_explanation:
The Press Freedom Index is published annually by Reporters Without Borders (RSF — Reporters Sans Frontières), a Paris-based NGO founded in 1985. It is not a UN or intergovernmental product, though it is cited in international discourse.

• Assertion (A): Correct. RSF publishes the Press Freedom Index using five criteria: political context, legal framework, economic context, sociocultural context, and safety of journalists.
• Reason (R): Correct. India's government has consistently challenged the index's methodology, arguing that it relies on subjective perceptions and questionnaire-based assessments rather than objective press freedom metrics.
• Causal link: R does not explain A. India's methodological objections are a response to the index's findings, not a factor that determines who publishes it. The two facts are independent.

Correct option: b — Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

Value Addition:
• RSF is distinct from Freedom House, which publishes 'Freedom of the Press' and 'Freedom in the World' — two separate products.
• India has ranked in the 150s range in recent PFI editions.
• RSF's five criteria include both quantitative and qualitative components.

solution.strong_distractor: c — Option c (UNEP's Global Environment Outlook) is the strongest distractor because UNEP is the most prominent UN body associated with environmental assessment, making students assume UNEP publishes EPI.
elimination_logic: Identify the shared category: options a, c, and d involve intergovernmental or academic bodies publishing recognised environmental assessments.
Option b states EPI is a UNEP product — but EPI is published by Yale and Columbia Universities, not UNEP.
Options a (UNEP-GEO), c (WHO air quality guidelines), and d (IPCC reports) are correctly attributed to their respective publishers.
The odd one out is option b — incorrect attribution of EPI to UNEP.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Students associate environmental performance assessment with UNEP — the UN's designated environmental programme. The actual publisher of EPI is a consortium of Yale University and Columbia University, operating independently of UNEP. India ranked 180th (last) in the 2022 EPI, and the government's strong rejection of the methodology — particularly the air quality weighting — is a tested controversy. Confusing UNEP's GEO report with the EPI is the core trap.
solution.final_explanation:
The Environmental Performance Index is published biennially by Yale University and Columbia University in collaboration with the World Economic Forum — not by UNEP. This is a frequently tested distinction.

• Option (a) — UNEP publishes Global Environment Outlook: Correct attribution. GEO is UNEP's flagship assessment.
• Option (b) — UNEP publishes Environmental Performance Index: Incorrect. EPI is published by Yale and Columbia Universities. This is the odd one out.
• Option (c) — WHO issues air quality guidelines: Correct attribution. WHO's Global Air Quality Guidelines are a separate product.
• Option (d) — IPCC publishes Assessment Reports: Correct attribution. IPCC's Assessment Reports are the gold standard for climate science.

Value Addition:
• India ranked 180th (last among 180 countries) in EPI 2022 — primarily due to air quality scoring.
• EPI covers 32 indicators under two objectives: Environmental Health and Ecosystem Vitality.
• India's government rejected EPI 2022 findings, arguing the air quality metrics used modelled data rather than ground-level monitoring.

solution.concept_anchor: GGGI vs GII — different publishers, different measurement focus

statement_analysis.statement: The Global Gender Gap Index published by the World Economic Forum measures gender parity rather than absolute levels of development, meaning a country could achieve a high score even if absolute educational attainment is low, provided female and male attainment levels are similar.
statement_analysis.reason: GGGI explicitly measures the gap (parity) between men and women across four sub-indices — it does not reward absolute achievement, only equal distribution between genders.

statement_analysis.statement: The Gender Inequality Index, which is a product of the World Economic Forum, evaluates inequality in three dimensions: reproductive health, empowerment, and labour market participation.
statement_analysis.reason: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) is published by UNDP as part of the Human Development Report — not by WEF. The three dimensions described (reproductive health, empowerment, labour market) are correct for GII but the publisher attribution is wrong.

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a (both correct) is the strongest distractor because the three GII dimensions listed in statement 2 are factually accurate, tempting students to overlook the incorrect publisher attribution.
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: GGGI measures parity (gap), not absolute levels — a country with low but equal female-male education scores well. Statement 1 is correct.
Verify statement 2: GII is published by UNDP/HDR, not WEF. WEF publishes GGGI, not GII. The publisher attribution in statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 correct + Statement 2 incorrect → option c.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 contains a precise factual description of the Gender Inequality Index's three dimensions (reproductive health, empowerment, labour market) — all of which are accurate. The trap is in the publisher attribution: students who know these three dimensions from GII methodology assume the full statement is correct, missing that the publisher is UNDP (via HDR), not WEF. WEF publishes GGGI; UNDP publishes GII — a conflation trap that exploits partial knowledge.
solution.final_explanation:
Two distinct gender indices dominate UPSC questions: the Global Gender Gap Index (GGGI) by WEF and the Gender Inequality Index (GII) by UNDP.

• Statement 1 — Correct: GGGI measures the gap between male and female outcomes, not absolute levels. Under its educational attainment sub-index, a country achieves parity when female and male literacy/enrolment rates are equal — regardless of how low they are in absolute terms. This explains why some low-income countries rank above wealthier nations on GGGI.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The three dimensions listed (reproductive health, empowerment, labour market participation) belong correctly to GII. However, GII is published by UNDP through the Human Development Report — not by WEF. WEF publishes GGGI with four sub-indices: economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment.

Value Addition:
• India's weakest GGGI sub-indices are Economic participation and Health and survival.
• GII score of 0 indicates perfect equality; 1 indicates complete inequality.
• Both indices appear in the same news cycle, making publisher confusion a recurring UPSC trap.

• कथन 1 — सही: GGGI पुरुष और महिला के बीच अंतर को मापता है, पूर्ण स्तर को नहीं। इसके शैक्षिक उपलब्धि उप-सूचकांक के तहत, जब महिला और पुरुष साक्षरता/नामांकन दरें समान होती हैं, तो देश समानता प्राप्त करता है — चाहे वे पूर्ण स्तर में कितनी भी कम क्यों न हों। यही कारण है कि कुछ कम आय वाले देश GGGI में अमीर देशों से ऊपर रैंक करते हैं।
• कथन 2 — गलत: सूचीबद्ध तीन आयाम (प्रजनन स्वास्थ्य, सशक्तिकरण, श्रम बाजार भागीदारी) सही रूप से GII के हैं। लेकिन GII UNDP द्वारा मानव विकास रिपोर्ट के माध्यम से प्रकाशित होता है — WEF द्वारा नहीं। WEF GGGI प्रकाशित करता है जिसमें चार उप-सूचकांक होते हैं: आर्थिक भागीदारी, शैक्षिक उपलब्धि, स्वास्थ्य और जीवित रहना, और राजनीतिक सशक्तिकरण।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• भारत के सबसे कमजोर GGGI उप-सूचकांक आर्थिक भागीदारी और स्वास्थ्य एवं जीवित रहना हैं।
• GII का स्कोर 0 पूर्ण समानता और 1 पूर्ण असमानता को दर्शाता है।
• दोनों सूचकांक एक ही समाचार चक्र में आते हैं, जिससे प्रकाशक भ्रम UPSC में बार-बार होता है।

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a is deceptive because the Basel AML Index and Basel Institute on Governance are correctly associated, and students unfamiliar with the precise distinction may accept this as the correct pair.
elimination_logic: Test option a: Basel AML Index is published by the Basel Institute on Governance — this is correct. But the question asks for the correct pair overall; continue checking.

Test option b: Financial Secrecy Index described as measuring 'money laundering risk' — incorrect. FSI measures offshore financial secrecy provisions, not money laundering risk exposure. This is wrong.
Test option c: Tax Justice Network publishes the Financial Secrecy Index — this is factually correct. Pair is valid.
Test option d: FATF mutual evaluation reports are produced by FATF itself, not by the Basel Institute. This pair is incorrect.
Only option c correctly matches the FSI with Tax Justice Network.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Both the Financial Secrecy Index and Basel AML Index deal with illicit finance but measure conceptually opposite things: the FSI measures how much secrecy a jurisdiction provides to offshore financial flows (higher secrecy = worse), while the Basel AML Index measures a country's risk of money laundering and terrorist financing (higher score = higher risk). Conflating these two instruments is the central trap. Additionally, attributing FSI to Basel Institute (instead of Tax Justice Network) is a common entity-swap error.
solution.final_explanation:
Two distinct indices cover illicit financial flows — the Financial Secrecy Index and the Basel AML Index — and they measure different dimensions with different publishers.

• Option (a) — Basel AML Index / Basel Institute on Governance: The publisher is correct (Basel Institute), but the question asks for the correct match — this pair is accurate. However, option c is the intended testable correct pair.
• Option (b) — FSI measures money laundering risk: Incorrect. FSI measures offshore financial secrecy — how much secrecy a jurisdiction affords. Money laundering risk is Basel AML's domain.
• Option (c) — FSI published by Tax Justice Network: Correct. Tax Justice Network, a UK-based civil society organisation, publishes the Financial Secrecy Index.
• Option (d) — FATF mutual evaluations published by Basel Institute: Incorrect. FATF mutual evaluations are conducted and published by FATF itself.

Value Addition:
• India is a FATF member; FATF mutual evaluations assess AML/CFT compliance independently of both FSI and Basel AML Index.
• A high FSI score means a jurisdiction is highly secretive; a high Basel AML score means high money laundering risk.
• Tax Justice Network also publishes the Corporate Tax Haven Index — a separate product.

solution.final_explanation:

• Statement 2 — Correct: India's worst-performing SDGs include SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

Three statements correct → option c (Only three).

• India's VNR submissions to HLPF have been made multiple times — VNRs are not mandatory.
• NITI Aayog's SDG India Index categorises states as Achiever, Front Runner, Performer, or Aspirant.
• The global SDG Index score is expressed as 0–100, with 100 indicating full achievement of all SDGs.

solution.final_explanation:
WIPO publishes two major annual products that are often confused: the Global Innovation Index (measuring innovation ecosystems) and the World Intellectual Property Indicators (measuring IP filing activity — patents, trademarks, industrial designs).

• Option (a) — Global Innovation Index: Incorrect for this question. GII focuses on innovation ecosystem indicators, not patent/trademark filing statistics. It is a separate WIPO product.
• Option (b) — PCT Applications Report: Incorrect as a standalone product name. PCT application data is part of WIPI's coverage but not a separate publication in the context being tested.
• Option (c) — World Intellectual Property Indicators (WIPI): Correct. WIPI is the WIPO publication covering patent filings (resident vs non-resident), trademark applications, industrial design filings, and related IP activity data.
• Option (d) — UNCTAD IP Competitiveness Report: Incorrect. UNCTAD does not publish this; it focuses on trade, investment, and development.

solution.concept_anchor: WIPO publishes GII and WIPI — two distinct products
solution.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प a भ्रामक है क्योंकि जो छात्र जानते हैं कि WIPO ग्लोबल इनोवेशन इंडेक्स प्रकाशित करता है, वे मान सकते हैं कि नवाचार और आईपी से संबंधित सभी WIPO उत्पाद एक साथ हैं, जिससे GII और World Intellectual Property Indicators के बीच अंतर छूट जाता है।
elimination_logic: विकल्प a को हटाएं: GII एक अलग WIPO उत्पाद है — यह नवाचार पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र पर केंद्रित है, न कि पेटेंट/ट्रेडमार्क फाइलिंग आंकड़ों पर।
विकल्प b को हटाएं: पेटेंट सहयोग संधि (PCT) आवेदन पर रिपोर्ट WIPI डेटा का एक घटक है लेकिन यह एक स्वतंत्र अलग प्रकाशन नहीं है; WIPI इसे समाहित करता है।
विकल्प c को बनाए रखें: World Intellectual Property Indicators (WIPI) सही WIPO प्रकाशन है जो पेटेंट, ट्रेडमार्क, और औद्योगिक डिज़ाइन फाइलिंग को कवर करता है।
विकल्प d को हटाएं: UNCTAD आईपी फाइलिंग आंकड़े प्रकाशित नहीं करता — यह व्यापार और निवेश प्रवाह को कवर करता है।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: WIPO दो अलग-अलग प्रमुख वार्षिक उत्पाद प्रकाशित करता है: ग्लोबल इनोवेशन इंडेक्स (INSEAD और कॉर्नेल के साथ सह-प्रकाशित) और World Intellectual Property Indicators (एक स्वतंत्र WIPO सांख्यिकीय प्रकाशन)। जो छात्र WIPO को नवाचार सूचकांकों से जोड़ते हैं, वे इन दोनों को मिलाकर समझते हैं, यह मानते हुए कि आईपी से संबंधित कोई भी WIPO प्रकाशन GII है। WIPI विशेष रूप से पेटेंट, ट्रेडमार्क, औद्योगिक डिज़ाइन, और पौधा विविधता फाइलिंग पर कठोर सांख्यिकीय डेटा कवर करता है — जो GII के नवाचार पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र मूल्यांकन से अलग है।
solution.final_explanation:
WIPO दो प्रमुख वार्षिक उत्पाद प्रकाशित करता है जिन्हें अक्सर भ्रमित किया जाता है: ग्लोबल इनोवेशन इंडेक्स (जो नवाचार पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र को मापता है) और World Intellectual Property Indicators (जो आईपी फाइलिंग गतिविधि — पेटेंट, ट्रेडमार्क, औद्योगिक डिज़ाइन — को मापता है)।

• विकल्प (a) — ग्लोबल इनोवेशन इंडेक्स: इस प्रश्न के लिए गलत। GII नवाचार पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र संकेतकों पर केंद्रित है, न कि पेटेंट/ट्रेडमार्क फाइलिंग आंकड़ों पर। यह एक अलग WIPO उत्पाद है।
• विकल्प (b) — PCT आवेदन वार्षिक रिपोर्ट: स्वतंत्र उत्पाद नाम के रूप में गलत। PCT आवेदन डेटा WIPI के कवरेज का हिस्सा है लेकिन परीक्षण संदर्भ में यह एक अलग प्रकाशन नहीं है।
• विकल्प (c) — World Intellectual Property Indicators (WIPI): सही। WIPI वह WIPO प्रकाशन है जो पेटेंट फाइलिंग (निवासी बनाम गैर-निवासी), ट्रेडमार्क आवेदन, औद्योगिक डिज़ाइन फाइलिंग, और संबंधित आईपी गतिविधि डेटा को कवर करता है।
• विकल्प (d) — UNCTAD आईपी प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता रिपोर्ट: गलत। UNCTAD इसे प्रकाशित नहीं करता; यह व्यापार, निवेश, और विकास पर केंद्रित है।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• भारत में पेटेंट फाइलिंग में वृद्धि निवासी फाइलिंग (घरेलू आविष्कारक) और गैर-निवासी फाइलिंग के बीच भेद करती है — भारत की निवासी फाइलिंग में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि हुई है।
• राष्ट्रीय आईपीआर नीति 2016 'क्रिएटिव इंडिया, इनोवेटिव इंडिया' ढांचे के अंतर्गत संचालित होती है।
• PCT आवेदन एकल आवेदन के माध्यम से कई सदस्य देशों में एक साथ पेटेंट संरक्षण की अनुमति देते हैं।

solution.concept_anchor: Fragile States Index — former name Failed States Index, 2014 name change

statement_analysis.statement: The Fragile States Index was formerly known as the Failed States Index, and this name change occurred in 2014.
statement_analysis.reason: Fund for Peace renamed the Failed States Index to Fragile States Index in 2014 to better reflect the nuanced spectrum of state fragility beyond outright failure.

statement_analysis.statement: The Fragile States Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and uses 12 indicators to assess state fragility.
statement_analysis.reason: The FSI is published by Fund for Peace (FFP), a US-based NGO — not UNDP. The 12 indicators across Cohesion, Economic, Political, and Social categories are correctly stated, but the publisher attribution is wrong.

statement_analysis.statement: India is classified in the 'Elevated Warning' category of the Fragile States Index, which is distinct from the more severe 'Alert' category.
statement_analysis.reason: India's FSI classification is 'Elevated Warning' — below the 'High Warning' and 'Alert' (most fragile) categories, reflecting significant but not crisis-level fragility indicators.

solution.strong_distractor: d — Option d (1, 2, and 3) is the strongest distractor because both the name change year (statement 1) and the 12-indicator structure (embedded in statement 2) are accurate, tempting students to overlook the publisher error.
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: Failed States Index → Fragile States Index name change occurred in 2014. Statement 1 is correct.
Test statement 2: FSI publisher is Fund for Peace (FFP), not UNDP. Despite the 12-indicator count being correct, the publisher is wrong. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Verify statement 3: India's 'Elevated Warning' classification and its distinction from 'Alert' is accurate. Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 1 and 3 correct; statement 2 incorrect → option c (1 and 3 only).
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 embeds a publisher trap inside otherwise accurate content. The 12-indicator structure of the FSI is correct — four categories (Cohesion, Economic, Political, Social) with three indicators each — but attributing it to UNDP is the deliberate error. UNDP is the most prominent development-focused UN body, making the attribution feel plausible to students who haven't specifically memorised that Fund for Peace (FFP) is the publisher.
solution.final_explanation:
The Fragile States Index (FSI) is published by Fund for Peace (FFP), an independent US-based research NGO — not a UN body. This distinction matters for UPSC questions that test publisher attribution.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The index was published as the 'Failed States Index' until 2014, when Fund for Peace rebranded it to 'Fragile States Index' to convey spectrum-based assessment rather than binary failure.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Fund for Peace, not UNDP, publishes the FSI. The 12-indicator count is accurate — covering Security Apparatus, Factionalised Elites, Group Grievance (Cohesion); Economy, Uneven Development, Human Flight (Economic); State Legitimacy, Public Services, Human Rights (Political); and Demographic Pressures, Refugees, External Intervention (Social).
• Statement 3 — Correct: India's FSI classification is 'Elevated Warning' — a middle tier, not the most severe 'Alert' or 'High Alert' categories.

Value Addition:
• FSI categories in descending severity: Very High Alert → High Alert → Alert → High Warning → Warning → Elevated Warning → Warning → Stable → Very Stable → Sustainable.
• Somalia, Yemen, and South Sudan have historically occupied top 'Alert' positions.
• The 2014 name change reflects academic consensus that state fragility is a continuum, not a binary condition.

solution.final_explanation:
Fragile States Index (FSI) को Fund for Peace (FFP), एक स्वतंत्र अमेरिकी आधारित अनुसंधान NGO द्वारा प्रकाशित किया जाता है — यह कोई UN संस्था नहीं है। यह भेद UPSC के उन प्रश्नों के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है जो प्रकाशक की पहचान पर आधारित होते हैं।

• कथन 1 — सही: यह सूचकांक 2014 तक 'Failed States Index' के नाम से प्रकाशित होता था, जब Fund for Peace ने इसे 'Fragile States Index' में बदल दिया ताकि द्विआधारी विफलता के बजाय स्पेक्ट्रम आधारित मूल्यांकन को दर्शाया जा सके।
• कथन 2 — गलत: FSI को Fund for Peace प्रकाशित करता है, न कि UNDP। 12-संकेतक की संख्या सही है — जिसमें Security Apparatus, Factionalised Elites, Group Grievance (Cohesion); Economy, Uneven Development, Human Flight (Economic); State Legitimacy, Public Services, Human Rights (Political); और Demographic Pressures, Refugees, External Intervention (Social) शामिल हैं।
• कथन 3 — सही: भारत की FSI वर्गीकरण 'Elevated Warning' है — जो मध्य स्तर है, न कि सबसे गंभीर 'Alert' या 'High Alert' श्रेणियाँ।

मूल्यवर्धन:
• FSI की श्रेणियाँ गंभीरता के अनुसार: Very High Alert → High Alert → Alert → High Warning → Warning → Elevated Warning → Warning → Stable → Very Stable → Sustainable।
• सोमालिया, यमन, और दक्षिण सूडान ने ऐतिहासिक रूप से शीर्ष 'Alert' स्थिति में स्थान पाया है।
• 2014 का नाम परिवर्तन इस अकादमिक सहमति को दर्शाता है कि राज्य की नाजुकता एक सतत प्रक्रिया है, द्विआधारी स्थिति नहीं।

solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The energy reporting landscape has multiple publishers, and UPSC exploits the tendency to attribute all energy transition reports to IEA. The ETI is a WEF product; the World Energy Outlook belongs to IEA; the Global Status Report belongs to REN21; and IRENA covers renewable energy capacity statistics. Students who know IEA's World Energy Outlook correctly may then incorrectly assign ETI to IEA, since both are 'energy transition' adjacent.
solution.final_explanation:
Four organisations publish major energy-related reports, each with a distinct focus and mandate.

• A (ETI) → 3 (WEF): The Energy Transition Index is a WEF product measuring progress on energy transition across equity, security, and sustainability dimensions.
• B (World Energy Outlook) → 1 (IEA): The International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook is the most authoritative annual global energy forecast, covering supply, demand, and policy scenarios.
• C (Global Status Report on Renewables) → 4 (REN21): REN21 (a global multi-stakeholder network) publishes this annual review of the renewable energy sector's status worldwide.
• D (Renewable Energy Statistics) → 2 (IRENA): The International Renewable Energy Agency publishes comprehensive capacity and generation data annually.

Correct match: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2 → option a.

Value Addition:
• India ranks globally in the top 4 in installed renewable energy capacity — but per capita renewable consumption remains low.
• IRENA and IEA are intergovernmental bodies; REN21 is a multi-stakeholder network; WEF is a non-profit foundation.
• ETI measures transition readiness across three dimensions: energy security, energy equity, and environmental sustainability.

solution.concept_anchor: कई ऊर्जा रिपोर्ट प्रकाशक — WEF ETI बनाम IEA बनाम IRENA बनाम REN21
solution.strong_distractor: b — विकल्प b गलत तरीके से ETI को IEA से जोड़ता है, जो एक संभावित त्रुटि है क्योंकि IEA सबसे प्रमुख ऊर्जा-केंद्रित अंतरसरकारी संस्था है और छात्र मान सकते हैं कि सभी प्रमुख ऊर्जा संक्रमण रिपोर्ट IEA से आती हैं।
elimination_logic: एंकर: एनर्जी ट्रांजिशन इंडेक्स (ETI) → WEF। WEF अपनी ऊर्जा प्लेटफॉर्म के हिस्से के रूप में ETI प्रकाशित करता है। A→3।
एंकर: वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक → IEA। IEA की प्रमुख वार्षिक प्रकाशन वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक है। B→1।
सत्यापित करें: ग्लोबल स्टेटस रिपोर्ट ऑन रिन्यूएबल्स → REN21। REN21 (Renewable Energy Policy Network for the 21st Century) वार्षिक ग्लोबल स्टेटस रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करता है। C→4।
सत्यापित करें: रिन्यूएबल एनर्जी स्टैटिस्टिक्स → IRENA। IRENA वार्षिक रिन्यूएबल एनर्जी स्टैटिस्टिक्स — क्षमता और उत्पादन डेटा प्रकाशित करता है। D→2।
पूर्ण मेल: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2 → विकल्प a।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: ऊर्जा रिपोर्टिंग क्षेत्र में कई प्रकाशक हैं, और UPSC इस प्रवृत्ति का लाभ उठाता है कि सभी ऊर्जा संक्रमण रिपोर्ट IEA को ही मान लिया जाए। ETI WEF का उत्पाद है; वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक IEA का है; ग्लोबल स्टेटस रिपोर्ट REN21 की है; और IRENA नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा क्षमता सांख्यिकी को कवर करता है। जो छात्र IEA के वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक को सही जानते हैं, वे गलत तरीके से ETI को IEA से जोड़ सकते हैं क्योंकि दोनों 'ऊर्जा संक्रमण' से संबंधित हैं।
solution.final_explanation:
चार संगठन प्रमुख ऊर्जा-संबंधित रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करते हैं, प्रत्येक का एक विशिष्ट फोकस और प्राधिकरण है।

• A (ETI) → 3 (WEF): एनर्जी ट्रांजिशन इंडेक्स WEF का उत्पाद है जो ऊर्जा संक्रमण की प्रगति को ऊर्जा सुरक्षा, ऊर्जा समानता, और पर्यावरणीय स्थिरता के आयामों में मापता है।
• B (वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक) → 1 (IEA): इंटरनेशनल एनर्जी एजेंसी की वर्ल्ड एनर्जी आउटलुक सबसे प्रामाणिक वार्षिक वैश्विक ऊर्जा पूर्वानुमान है, जो आपूर्ति, मांग, और नीति परिदृश्यों को कवर करता है।
• C (ग्लोबल स्टेटस रिपोर्ट ऑन रिन्यूएबल्स) → 4 (REN21): REN21 (एक वैश्विक बहु-हितधारक नेटवर्क) वार्षिक रूप से नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा क्षेत्र की स्थिति की समीक्षा प्रकाशित करता है।
• D (रिन्यूएबल एनर्जी स्टैटिस्टिक्स) → 2 (IRENA): इंटरनेशनल रिन्यूएबल एनर्जी एजेंसी वार्षिक रूप से व्यापक क्षमता और उत्पादन डेटा प्रकाशित करता है।

सही मिलान: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2 → विकल्प a।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• भारत वैश्विक स्तर पर स्थापित नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा क्षमता में शीर्ष 4 में है — लेकिन प्रति व्यक्ति नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा खपत अभी भी कम है।
• IRENA और IEA अंतरसरकारी संस्थाएं हैं; REN21 एक बहु-हितधारक नेटवर्क है; WEF एक गैर-लाभकारी फाउंडेशन है।
• ETI तीन आयामों में संक्रमण की तत्परता को मापता है: ऊर्जा सुरक्षा, ऊर्जा समानता, और पर्यावरणीय स्थिरता।

solution.concept_anchor: TB elimination target — India 2025 vs global 2030
solution.strong_distractor: c — Option c (STOP TB Partnership) is deceptive because it is a legitimate TB-related multilateral mechanism, making it sound like an appropriate answer for financing TB elimination goals.
elimination_logic: The scenario asks which combination correctly pairs India's TB elimination target with the global target and the reporting agency.
India's TB-Mukt Bharat targets 2025 elimination; the global End TB Strategy targets 2030 — this asymmetry is key.
WHO publishes the Global TB Report annually — not SDSN, not STOP TB Partnership.
Only option b correctly states India 2025 + global 2030 + WHO as the reporting body.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The most common trap is confusing India's TB elimination target (2025) with the global target (2030). Both are widely cited but represent different timelines. India has committed to eliminating TB five years ahead of the global target under 'TB-Mukt Bharat.' Students who recall only one of these dates tend to select an incorrect option. The secondary trap is attributing TB reporting to STOP TB Partnership or SDSN rather than WHO.
solution.final_explanation:
India's TB burden is a recurring UPSC topic at the intersection of public health, global indices, and SDG framework. The WHO publishes the Global TB Report annually, tracking incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates across 194 member states.

• Option (a) — India 2030 / Global 2025 / WHO: Incorrect. The targets are reversed. India committed to 2025; global target is 2030.
• Option (b) — India 2025 / Global 2030 / WHO: Correct. India's 'TB-Mukt Bharat' targets 2025 elimination (5 years ahead of the global End TB Strategy's 2030 goal). WHO is the correct reporting body.
• Option (c) — India 2025 / Global 2030 / STOP TB Partnership: Incorrect on the publisher. STOP TB Partnership is a global coalition supporting TB elimination but does not publish the Global TB Report.
• Option (d) — India 2025 / Global 2035 / WHO: Incorrect. The global target is 2030 under End TB Strategy — not 2035.

Value Addition:
• India accounts for approximately 26% of global TB burden — the highest of any single country.
• 'Elimination' in public health terminology means fewer than 1 case per 1,000,000 population.
• Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria finances TB programmes but is distinct from WHO's reporting function.

elimination_logic: परिदृश्य पूछता है कि कौन सा संयोजन सही ढंग से भारत के टीबी उन्मूलन लक्ष्य को वैश्विक लक्ष्य और रिपोर्टिंग एजेंसी के साथ जोड़ता है।
भारत का टीबी-मुक्त भारत लक्ष्य 2025 है; वैश्विक End TB Strategy का लक्ष्य 2030 है — यह असममिति महत्वपूर्ण है।
WHO वार्षिक रूप से Global TB Report प्रकाशित करता है — न कि SDSN, न ही STOP TB Partnership।
केवल विकल्प b सही रूप से भारत 2025 + वैश्विक 2030 + WHO को रिपोर्टिंग संस्था के रूप में बताता है।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: सबसे आम जाल भारत के टीबी उन्मूलन लक्ष्य (2025) को वैश्विक लक्ष्य (2030) से भ्रमित करना है। दोनों व्यापक रूप से उद्धृत हैं लेकिन अलग-अलग समयरेखा दर्शाते हैं। भारत ने 'टीबी-मुक्त भारत' के तहत वैश्विक लक्ष्य से पांच साल पहले 2025 तक टीबी उन्मूलन का संकल्प लिया है। जो छात्र केवल एक तारीख याद रखते हैं, वे गलत विकल्प चुनते हैं। दूसरा जाल यह है कि टीबी रिपोर्टिंग को STOP TB Partnership या SDSN को देना बजाय WHO के।
solution.final_explanation:
भारत का टीबी बोझ सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य, वैश्विक सूचकांक, और SDG फ्रेमवर्क के संगम पर एक बार-बार आने वाला UPSC विषय है। WHO वार्षिक रूप से Global TB Report प्रकाशित करता है, जो 194 सदस्य राज्यों में टीबी की घटना, प्रचलन, और मृत्यु दर को ट्रैक करता है।

• विकल्प (a) — भारत 2030 / वैश्विक 2025 / WHO: गलत। लक्ष्य उलटे हैं। भारत ने 2025 का संकल्प लिया है; वैश्विक लक्ष्य 2030 है।
• विकल्प (b) — भारत 2025 / वैश्विक 2030 / WHO: सही। भारत का 'टीबी-मुक्त भारत' 2025 तक उन्मूलन का लक्ष्य रखता है (वैश्विक End TB Strategy के 2030 लक्ष्य से 5 साल पहले)। WHO सही रिपोर्टिंग संस्था है।

• विकल्प (d) — भारत 2025 / वैश्विक 2035 / WHO: गलत। वैश्विक लक्ष्य End TB Strategy के तहत 2030 है — 2035 नहीं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• भारत वैश्विक टीबी बोझ का लगभग 26% हिस्सा रखता है — जो किसी भी एकल देश में सबसे अधिक है।
• सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य शब्दावली में 'उन्मूलन' का अर्थ है प्रति 1,000,000 आबादी में 1 से कम मामले।
• Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria टीबी कार्यक्रमों को वित्तपोषित करता है लेकिन WHO की रिपोर्टिंग कार्य से अलग है।

solution.concept_anchor: GHI four indicators — weightage distribution trap
solution.strong_distractor: b — Option b (child stunting) is deceptive because stunting is a prominent nutrition metric and students may assume it carries the highest weight given its visibility in nutrition discourse.
elimination_logic: GHI has four indicators with specific weightages: undernourishment (1/3), child wasting (1/6), child stunting (1/6), child mortality (1/3).
Options a, b, and d are correctly identified as components of GHI — undernourishment, child stunting, and child mortality are all valid GHI indicators.
Option c states 'maternal anaemia rate' — this is NOT a GHI indicator. GHI does not include maternal anaemia in its four-indicator framework.
The odd one out is option c — maternal anaemia rate.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Maternal anaemia is a prominent nutrition and public health indicator tracked by WHO and NFHS, and appears frequently alongside hunger discussions. Students who associate anaemia with nutritional deprivation (a theme central to GHI) may accept it as a GHI component. The actual four GHI indicators are restricted to undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting, and child mortality — maternal anaemia is a distractor drawn from adjacent nutritional discourse.
solution.final_explanation:
The Global Hunger Index uses exactly four indicators to compute its composite score, each with a defined weightage.

• Option (a) — Undernourishment: Correct GHI indicator. Carries 1/3 weight. Measured using FAO modelled estimates of caloric intake insufficiency.
• Option (b) — Child stunting: Correct GHI indicator. Carries 1/6 weight. Measures the proportion of children under five who are too short for their age.
• Option (c) — Maternal anaemia rate: NOT a GHI indicator. This is the odd one out. GHI does not incorporate maternal anaemia — this metric appears in NFHS data and WHO nutrition reports but not in the four-indicator GHI framework.
• Option (d) — Child mortality: Correct GHI indicator. Carries 1/3 weight. Measures mortality rate of children under five.

Value Addition:
• Child wasting (also 1/6 weight) measures proportion of children under five who are too thin for their height — acute malnutrition.
• The two heaviest-weighted components (undernourishment + child mortality) together account for 2/3 of the GHI score.
• India objects to GHI's reliance on Gallup opinion polls for the undernourishment component.

• विकल्प (d) — बाल मृत्यु दर: सही GHI संकेतक। 1/3 भार। पाँच वर्ष से कम उम्र के बच्चों की मृत्यु दर मापता है।

solution.concept_anchor: CPI measures public sector perception only — private sector excluded

statement_analysis.statement: The Corruption Perceptions Index published by Transparency International measures the perceived level of corruption in the public sector only and does not assess actual corruption incidents or private sector corruption.
statement_analysis.reason: CPI is explicitly restricted to public sector corruption perception — it is perception-based (not incident-based) and private sector corruption is outside its methodological scope.

statement_analysis.statement: A country whose CPI score improves over a given year will necessarily also improve its CPI rank in the same year.
statement_analysis.reason: Score improvement does not guarantee rank improvement — if other countries improve their scores at a faster rate, a country's score can rise while its rank falls or stagnates. The score-rank divergence is a key CPI methodological point.

solution.strong_distractor: a — Students who correctly identify statement 1 as true may not carefully evaluate statement 2's conditional logic, defaulting to 'both correct' without testing the rank-score independence.
elimination_logic: Test statement 1: CPI measures only public sector corruption perception — private sector is excluded, and actual incidents are not measured. Statement 1 is correct.

Test statement 2: Score improvement does not necessarily mean rank improvement — rank is relative to all other countries. If others improve more, rank can decline despite score improvement. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 correct + Statement 2 incorrect → option c.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 exploits the intuitive assumption that a better score means a better rank — which would be true only in a fixed or isolated scoring system. CPI rank is relative: it depends on how all 180 countries score in any given year. A country can improve its absolute score and still drop in rank if other nations improve more rapidly. This score-vs-rank distinction is a canonical UPSC trap in index methodology questions.
solution.final_explanation:
The CPI's two key methodological limitations are precisely what UPSC tests: its restriction to public sector perception, and the non-linear relationship between score and rank.

• Statement 1 — Correct: CPI measures perceived corruption in the public sector — covering government officials, civil servants, and state institutions. Private sector corruption and actual prosecuted incidents are outside its scope. It aggregates data from 13 expert surveys.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: CPI rank is determined relative to all participating countries. If a country's score improves from 40 to 43 but the average improvement of other nations is larger, that country will fall in rank. Score and rank move independently depending on the competitive field.

Statement 1 correct + Statement 2 incorrect → option c.

Value Addition:
• CPI scores range from 0 (highly corrupt perception) to 100 (very clean perception).
• The 13 data sources include surveys by World Bank, WEF, Bertelsmann Stiftung, among others.
• Transparency International is headquartered in Berlin — it is a civil society organisation, not a UN body.

statement_analysis.statement: जिस देश का CPI स्कोर किसी दिए गए वर्ष में सुधरता है, उसका CPI रैंक उसी वर्ष में अवश्य सुधरेगा।
statement_analysis.reason: स्कोर में सुधार रैंक सुधार की गारंटी नहीं देता — यदि अन्य देश अपने स्कोर को तेज़ी से सुधारते हैं, तो किसी देश का स्कोर बढ़ने के बावजूद उसका रैंक गिर सकता है या स्थिर रह सकता है। स्कोर-रैंक असंगति CPI की कार्यप्रणाली का एक मुख्य बिंदु है।

solution.strong_distractor: a — जो छात्र कथन 1 को सही पहचानते हैं, वे कथन 2 की सशर्त तर्कशक्ति का सावधानीपूर्वक मूल्यांकन नहीं करते और बिना रैंक-स्कोर स्वतंत्रता की जांच किए 'दोनों सही' मान लेते हैं।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 का परीक्षण करें: CPI केवल सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र के भ्रष्टाचार की धारणा को मापता है — निजी क्षेत्र शामिल नहीं है, और वास्तविक घटनाओं को मापा नहीं जाता। कथन 1 सही है।

कथन 2 का परीक्षण करें: स्कोर में सुधार का मतलब जरूरी नहीं कि रैंक में सुधार हो — रैंक सभी अन्य देशों के सापेक्ष होता है। यदि अन्य देश अधिक सुधार करते हैं, तो रैंक गिर सकता है भले ही स्कोर बढ़ा हो। कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 1 सही + कथन 2 गलत → विकल्प c।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 उस सहज धारणा का फायदा उठाता है कि बेहतर स्कोर का मतलब बेहतर रैंक होता है — जो केवल एक स्थिर या पृथक स्कोरिंग प्रणाली में सही होगा। CPI रैंक सापेक्ष है: यह इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि किसी वर्ष में सभी 180 देश कैसे स्कोर करते हैं। कोई देश अपना पूर्णांक स्कोर सुधार सकता है और फिर भी रैंक में गिरावट आ सकती है यदि अन्य देश तेज़ी से सुधार करें। यह स्कोर-विरुद्ध-रैंक भेद UPSC के सूचकांक कार्यप्रणाली प्रश्नों में एक पारंपरिक जाल है।
solution.final_explanation:

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a is deceptive because it correctly names RSF as the publisher but attributes an incorrect number of criteria (three instead of five), which students may overlook if they only check the publisher.
elimination_logic: Test option a: RSF is correct as publisher, but PFI uses five criteria, not three. Pair is incorrect.
Test option b: RSF publishes PFI using five criteria (political context, legal framework, economic context, sociocultural context, safety). Both elements are correct. This is the correct pair.
Test option c: Freedom House does not publish PFI — it publishes Freedom of the Press and Freedom in the World. Incorrect attribution.
Test option d: The five criteria listed under Freedom House are actually RSF's criteria — conflation between two publishers. Incorrect.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Option a is the primary trap — it correctly identifies RSF as the publisher (which students who have studied the topic will confirm) but attaches an incorrect number of criteria (three instead of five). Students who anchor on publisher-identity rather than reading the complete pair will select option a. The correct pair (option b) requires verifying both the publisher and the exact count of five criteria.
solution.final_explanation:
The Press Freedom Index uses five evaluation criteria — a specific detail that UPSC has tested in the context of India's government disputing the index's subjective methodology.

• Option (a) — RSF / three criteria: Publisher is correct; criteria count is incorrect. PFI uses five criteria, not three.
• Option (b) — RSF / five criteria (political context, legal framework, economic context, sociocultural context, safety): Correct on both elements. This is the correctly matched pair.
• Option (c) — Freedom House / PFI: Incorrect publisher. Freedom House publishes 'Freedom of the Press' and 'Freedom in the World' — separate products with their own methodology.
• Option (d) — Freedom House / five RSF criteria: Conflation trap — the five criteria belong to RSF's PFI, not Freedom House's framework.

Value Addition:
• RSF was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Paris.
• Freedom House's Freedom in the World classifies countries as Free, Partly Free, or Not Free — different from RSF's numerical ranking.
• India's government has specifically objected to the 'safety' and 'political context' criteria in RSF's methodology as subjectively weighted.

solution.upsc_trap_explanation: विकल्प a मुख्य जाल है — यह सही रूप से RSF को प्रकाशक के रूप में पहचानता है (जिसकी पुष्टि विषय पढ़ने वाले छात्र करेंगे) लेकिन गलत संख्या में मानदंड (तीन के बजाय पाँच) जोड़ता है। जो छात्र केवल प्रकाशक की पहचान पर ध्यान केंद्रित करते हैं और पूरी जोड़ी नहीं पढ़ते, वे विकल्प a चुनेंगे। सही जोड़ी (विकल्प b) के लिए प्रकाशक और पाँच मानदंडों की सही संख्या दोनों की पुष्टि आवश्यक है।

• विकल्प (a) — RSF / तीन मानदंड: प्रकाशक सही है; मानदंड संख्या गलत है। PFI तीन नहीं, पाँच मानदंडों का उपयोग करता है।
• विकल्प (b) — RSF / पाँच मानदंड (राजनीतिक संदर्भ, कानूनी ढांचा, आर्थिक संदर्भ, सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक संदर्भ, सुरक्षा): दोनों तत्वों में सही। यह सही मेल वाली जोड़ी है।
• विकल्प (c) — Freedom House / PFI: गलत प्रकाशक। Freedom House 'Freedom of the Press' और 'Freedom in the World' प्रकाशित करता है — अलग उत्पाद जिनकी अपनी कार्यप्रणाली है।
• विकल्प (d) — Freedom House / पाँच RSF मानदंड: भ्रम जाल — ये पाँच मानदंड RSF के PFI के हैं, Freedom House के ढांचे के नहीं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• RSF की स्थापना 1985 में हुई थी और इसका मुख्यालय पेरिस में है।
• Freedom House का Freedom in the World देशों को Free, Partly Free, या Not Free के रूप में वर्गीकृत करता है — जो RSF की संख्यात्मक रैंकिंग से अलग है।
• भारत सरकार ने विशेष रूप से RSF की कार्यप्रणाली में 'सुरक्षा' और 'राजनीतिक संदर्भ' मानदंडों को विषयगत रूप से भारित होने के कारण आपत्ति जताई है।

statement_analysis.statement: India's government has disputed the Global Hunger Index methodology primarily on the ground that the undernourishment indicator relies on a sample-based opinion poll rather than objective nutritional surveys.
statement_analysis.reason: India's official objection to GHI focuses on the undernourishment component, which uses Gallup World Poll data from a sample of approximately 3,000 respondents — India argues this is too small and subjective to represent a country of 1.4 billion.

statement_analysis.statement: India ranked last among 180 countries in the Environmental Performance Index 2022 and the government's primary objection was to the index's overemphasis on air quality metrics derived from satellite-modelled data rather than ground monitoring.
statement_analysis.reason: India ranked 180th in EPI 2022; the government explicitly rejected the methodology citing excessive weight given to air quality indicators calculated from modelled (not ground-level) data.

statement_analysis.statement: Both the Global Hunger Index and the Environmental Performance Index are published by agencies of the United Nations system.
statement_analysis.reason: GHI is published by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe (NGOs); EPI is published by Yale and Columbia Universities — neither is a UN agency.

solution.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all three) is the primary trap because statements 1 and 2 are accurate and detailed, making students who have partially studied these controversies overlook statement 3's publisher error.
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: India's GHI objection centres on Gallup-based undernourishment data — correct.
Verify statement 2: India ranked 180th in EPI 2022; objection to satellite-modelled air quality data — correct.
Test statement 3: GHI publisher = Concern Worldwide + Welthungerhilfe (NGOs); EPI publisher = Yale + Columbia (universities). Neither is UN. Statement 3 is incorrect.
Statements 1 and 2 correct; statement 3 incorrect → option b (1 and 2 only).
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3 is a conflation trap that bundles two separate factual errors — attributing GHI to the UN system and attributing EPI to the UN system simultaneously. Students who have learned that 'India disputes indices published by international organisations' may loosely categorise both under 'UN/international bodies' without recalling the specific publishers. The trap is designed to test whether students have memorised publisher identity, not just the controversies.
solution.final_explanation:
India has formally disputed both GHI and EPI on methodological grounds — but these indices come from entirely different non-UN publishers.

• Statement 1 — Correct: India objects to GHI's undernourishment component, which uses Gallup World Poll data from a sample of ~3,000 respondents projected onto 1.4 billion people — an approach India calls statistically unreliable.
• Statement 2 — Correct: India's 180th rank in EPI 2022 triggered a government rebuttal specifically targeting air quality metrics derived from satellite modelling rather than ground-based monitoring stations, which India considers more accurate.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: GHI is a product of two European NGOs (Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe); EPI is published by Yale University and Columbia University. Neither belongs to the UN system.

Value Addition:
• The FAO State of Food Security report (UN body) and GHI (NGO) often reach different conclusions on India's hunger situation.
• UNEP's Global Environment Outlook (UN) is separate from EPI (Yale/Columbia).
• India's disputes with both indices highlight the methodological sovereignty debate in global indices.

solution.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 3 एक मिश्रण जाल है जो दो अलग-अलग तथ्यात्मक त्रुटियों को जोड़ता है — GHI को संयुक्त राष्ट्र प्रणाली से जोड़ना और EPI को संयुक्त राष्ट्र प्रणाली से जोड़ना एक साथ। जो छात्र यह जानते हैं कि 'भारत अंतरराष्ट्रीय संगठनों द्वारा प्रकाशित सूचकांकों को विवादित करता है' वे दोनों को 'संयुक्त राष्ट्र/अंतरराष्ट्रीय निकायों' के अंतर्गत ढेर कर सकते हैं बिना विशिष्ट प्रकाशकों को याद किए। यह जाल यह जांचने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है कि क्या छात्रों ने केवल विवादों को नहीं बल्कि प्रकाशक की पहचान को भी याद किया है।

solution.strong_distractor: b — Option b places the discontinuation before India's rank peak (63rd in 2020), which students who roughly recall 'India improved then EoDB was discontinued' may select without pinning the exact year order.
elimination_logic: India's EoDB baseline rank was 142nd in 2014 — this is the starting point of the reform narrative.

The data manipulation controversy was investigated and confirmed in 2021 — leading to discontinuation.
B-READY was announced as the replacement framework after the 2021 discontinuation.
Correct sequence: India rank 142nd (2014) → India rank 63rd (2020) → Discontinuation (2021) → B-READY announced → option d.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The year 2021 (discontinuation) and 2020 (India's last rank) are within one year of each other, making their sequence a classic temporal-swap trap. Students who recall India's improvement journey often anchor on 2019 or 2021 as the 'peak rank year' rather than 2020. The correct sequence requires knowing that the last published edition (Doing Business 2020) showed India at 63rd, and that the manipulation investigation and discontinuation came in 2021.
solution.final_explanation:
The EoDB story follows a clear timeline with four anchor points that UPSC has tested in various combinations.

Correct chronological sequence:
1. India's rank 142nd (2014) — starting point under new government's reform agenda.
2. India's rank 63rd (2020) — peak rank, recorded in the last published edition.
3. World Bank discontinues EoDB (2021) — following the WilmerHale investigation revealing manipulation in 2018 and 2020 editions.
4. B-READY framework announced — as the successor assessment tool with redesigned pillars.

This sequence corresponds to option d.

Value Addition:
• The data manipulation specifically affected rankings of China, Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Azerbaijan.
• India's 79-rank improvement (142→63) over six years is one of the most frequently cited reform achievements in government documents.
• B-READY stands for 'Business Ready' — it assesses regulatory environment, public services, and operational efficiency.
• Doing Business 2021 edition was never published — the series effectively ended with the 2020 data.

statement_analysis.statement: The Basel AML Index, published by the Basel Institute on Governance, measures the degree of financial secrecy that a jurisdiction provides to offshore capital flows.
statement_analysis.reason: The Basel AML Index measures money laundering and terrorist financing risk — not financial secrecy. Financial secrecy is measured by the Financial Secrecy Index published by Tax Justice Network. The two indices measure conceptually opposite dimensions.

statement_analysis.statement: India's FATF membership involves periodic mutual evaluation reviews that assess its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing frameworks — these evaluations are separate from the Basel AML Index.
statement_analysis.reason: FATF mutual evaluations are conducted by FATF and its peer review mechanism — they are independent of the Basel AML Index, though both cover AML/CFT compliance territory.

statement_analysis.statement: A high score on the Financial Secrecy Index indicates that a jurisdiction offers extensive secrecy to offshore financial flows, while a high score on the Basel AML Index indicates elevated risk of money laundering.
statement_analysis.reason: This correctly captures the directional meaning of both indices — FSI high score = more secrecy (negative); Basel AML high score = higher risk (negative). Both high scores are undesirable indicators.

solution.strong_distractor: b — Option b (statement 2 only) is the strongest distractor because students who correctly identify statement 1 as wrong may then doubt statement 3, which requires knowing the directional interpretation of both indices simultaneously.
elimination_logic: Test statement 1: Basel AML measures money laundering risk — NOT financial secrecy. Financial secrecy is the FSI's domain. Statement 1 is incorrect.
Verify statement 2: FATF mutual evaluations are a separate mechanism from Basel AML Index — both cover AML but are independent products. Statement 2 is correct.
Verify statement 3: FSI high = more secrecy; Basel AML high = higher risk. Both directional descriptions are accurate. Statement 3 is correct.
Only statement 1 is incorrect → option a (1 only) answers 'which is NOT correct.'
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The Basel-FSI conflation is a well-designed trap because both indices deal with illicit finance. Students who have memorised that 'Basel Institute + money laundering' is associated with the Basel AML Index may still confuse its directional measurement with FSI's secrecy-provision measurement. The key distinction is that FSI measures how much secrecy a jurisdiction affords (supply side), while Basel AML measures how exposed a jurisdiction is to money laundering risk (risk side).
solution.final_explanation:
The illicit finance index landscape has two distinct instruments that UPSC exploits for confusion.

• Statement 1 — Incorrect: The Basel AML Index measures money laundering and terrorist financing risk — NOT financial secrecy. Financial secrecy is the domain of the Financial Secrecy Index (Tax Justice Network). Swapping these two measurements is the central trap.
• Statement 2 — Correct: FATF mutual evaluation reviews are a peer-review mechanism operated by FATF — independent of the Basel AML Index. Both assess AML/CFT compliance but are separate institutional products.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Both high scores are undesirable — high FSI = jurisdiction enables offshore secrecy (problematic for transparency); high Basel AML = jurisdiction faces elevated money laundering risk.

Only statement 1 is incorrect → option a.

• Tax Justice Network also publishes the Corporate Tax Haven Index — a separate secrecy-adjacent product.
• FATF's 'grey list' and 'black list' (ISCO) are distinct from both FSI and Basel AML Index classifications.

solution.concept_anchor: WIPO's two distinct publications — GII and WIPI

statement_analysis.statement: WIPO publishes both the Global Innovation Index and the World Intellectual Property Indicators — these are two distinct annual publications with different methodological focus areas.
statement_analysis.reason: WIPO publishes GII (innovation ecosystem assessment) and WIPI (statistical tracking of patent, trademark, and design filings) — these are separate products with different methodologies and purposes.

statement_analysis.statement: India's Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) application count and its domestic patent filing count are identical, as both measure the same set of innovation activities.
statement_analysis.reason: PCT applications and domestic patent filings are entirely different categories — PCT applications seek international protection simultaneously in multiple countries, while domestic filings are restricted to the Indian Patent Office. India's rank differs significantly across these categories.

statement_analysis.statement: The National IPR Policy 2016 operates under the framework titled 'Creative India, Innovative India' and seeks to strengthen intellectual property creation and commercialisation.
statement_analysis.reason: India's National IPR Policy 2016 is officially branded as 'Creative India, Innovative India' — a correct attribution of the policy title and its broad mandate.

statement_analysis.statement: India's rank in patent filings in the WIPO data is the same whether measured by resident filings or total (resident + non-resident) filings.
statement_analysis.reason: Resident and total filing ranks differ substantially for India — resident filings (by Indian inventors at Indian Patent Office) and total filings (including foreign applicants in India) yield different country rankings.

solution.strong_distractor: d — Option d (all four correct) is the strongest distractor because statement 1 and statement 3 are clearly correct, tempting students who are unsure about statements 2 and 4 to select 'all four.'
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: WIPO publishes GII and WIPI as separate products — correct.
Test statement 2: PCT and domestic patent filings are distinct categories measuring different activities — statement 2 is incorrect.
Verify statement 3: National IPR Policy 2016 = 'Creative India, Innovative India' — correct.
Test statement 4: Resident filings and total filings yield different country ranks — statement 4 is incorrect.
Two statements correct (1 and 3), two incorrect (2 and 4) → option b (Only two).
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 is a scope-extension trap — it extends PCT and domestic filings as equivalent measures of 'the same set of innovation activities,' which is factually wrong. Statement 4 is a conflation trap — equating resident-only ranks with total-filing ranks. Together, these two incorrect statements are embedded in plausible-sounding language that only close reading can detect.
solution.final_explanation:
WIPO's two flagship publications — GII and WIPI — address different dimensions: innovation ecosystems versus IP filing statistics. Understanding the difference is crucial for answering WIPO-related UPSC questions.

• Statement 1 — Correct: GII measures the innovation ecosystem (institutions, human capital, outputs); WIPI measures IP filing activity (patents, trademarks, industrial designs). Both are annual WIPO publications.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: PCT applications and domestic patent filings measure different activities. PCT applications seek protection across multiple jurisdictions simultaneously; domestic filings cover only India. India ranks differently in each category.
• Statement 3 — Correct: National IPR Policy 2016 is titled 'Creative India, Innovative India' — a verifiable policy branding fact.
• Statement 4 — Incorrect: Resident filing rank (Indian inventors only) and total filing rank (resident + non-resident applicants) are different metrics yielding different country positions.

Two correct → option b (Only two).

Value Addition:
• India has emerged as a top-10 country in resident patent filings — a milestone cited in WIPO's WIPI reports.
• PCT membership allows Indian innovators to file a single application valid in 150+ countries.
• 'Creative India, Innovative India' also covers copyright, geographical indications, and traditional knowledge protection.

solution.concept_anchor: TB incidence vs prevalence vs mortality — definitional distinction

statement_analysis.statement: The incidence rate of tuberculosis refers to the number of new and relapse TB cases arising in a given year per 100,000 population, and is distinct from TB prevalence which measures the proportion of the population living with TB at any given point in time.
statement_analysis.reason: TB incidence (new and relapse cases per 100,000 per year) and prevalence (all existing cases at a point in time per 100,000) are definitionally distinct — this distinction is core to WHO's Global TB Report methodology.

statement_analysis.statement: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria is the body responsible for publishing the annual Global TB Report and tracking country-level TB incidence data.
statement_analysis.reason: The Global TB Report is published by WHO — not the Global Fund. The Global Fund is a financing mechanism that funds TB, AIDS, and malaria programmes; it does not produce the annual TB burden data report.

solution.strong_distractor: a — Option a (both correct) is the trap students who know statement 1 is accurate will select if they also incorrectly recall Global Fund as the TB reporting body.
elimination_logic: Verify statement 1: TB incidence = new + relapse cases per 100,000 per year; prevalence = all existing cases at a point in time per 100,000. Distinction is accurate. Statement 1 is correct.
Test statement 2: Global TB Report is a WHO publication — Global Fund is a financing body, not a reporting/data body. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 1 correct + Statement 2 incorrect → option c.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: The Global Fund and WHO are both prominent institutions in TB control discourse, appearing in the same news cycles and official documents. Students who know Global Fund is associated with TB may attribute publication of TB data to it, rather than correctly identifying WHO as the publisher. Statement 2 is a deliberate entity-swap embedded in an otherwise accurate-sounding sentence about tracking country-level TB burden.
solution.final_explanation:
WHO's Global TB Report is the authoritative annual publication tracking TB burden globally — distinct from the Global Fund, which finances TB programme delivery.

• Statement 1 — Correct: TB incidence rate counts new and relapse cases per 100,000 population per year; TB prevalence counts all existing cases (active TB) per 100,000 at a specific point in time. These are distinct epidemiological measures — UPSC has tested this definitional precision.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria is a multilateral financing mechanism — it does not publish epidemiological data or the Global TB Report. WHO publishes the annual Global TB Report.

Statement 1 correct + Statement 2 incorrect → option c.

Value Addition:
• India accounts for approximately 26% of global TB incidence — the highest national share.
• TB mortality rate refers to TB deaths per 100,000 population — a third distinct metric.
• India's 'TB-Mukt Bharat' target of 2025 elimination is based on achieving incidence below 1 per million — a public health elimination threshold.

solution.concept_anchor: टीबी घटना दर बनाम प्रचलन बनाम मृत्यु दर — परिभाषात्मक भेद

statement_analysis.statement: क्षय रोग की घटना दर उस वर्ष प्रति 100,000 जनसंख्या में उत्पन्न होने वाले नए और पुनरावर्ती टीबी मामलों की संख्या को दर्शाती है, और यह टीबी प्रचलन से भिन्न है जो किसी भी दिए गए समय पर टीबी से पीड़ित जनसंख्या के अनुपात को मापता है।
statement_analysis.reason: टीबी घटना (प्रति वर्ष प्रति 100,000 नए और पुनरावर्ती मामले) और प्रचलन (किसी बिंदु पर प्रति 100,000 सभी मौजूदा मामले) परिभाषात्मक रूप से भिन्न हैं — यह भेद WHO के ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट पद्धति का मूल है।

statement_analysis.statement: एड्स, क्षय रोग और मलेरिया से लड़ने के लिए ग्लोबल फंड वार्षिक ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करने और देश-स्तरीय टीबी घटना डेटा को ट्रैक करने वाला निकाय है।
statement_analysis.reason: ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट WHO द्वारा प्रकाशित की जाती है — ग्लोबल फंड नहीं। ग्लोबल फंड एक वित्तपोषण तंत्र है जो टीबी, एड्स और मलेरिया कार्यक्रमों को निधि प्रदान करता है; यह वार्षिक टीबी बोझ डेटा रिपोर्ट तैयार नहीं करता।

solution.strong_distractor: a — विकल्प a (दोनों सही) वह जाल है जिसे वे छात्र चुनेंगे जो जानते हैं कि कथन 1 सही है लेकिन गलती से ग्लोबल फंड को टीबी रिपोर्टिंग निकाय समझते हैं।
elimination_logic: कथन 1 सत्यापित करें: टीबी घटना = प्रति वर्ष प्रति 100,000 नए + पुनरावर्ती मामले; प्रचलन = किसी बिंदु पर प्रति 100,000 सभी मौजूदा मामले। भेद सही है। कथन 1 सही है।
कथन 2 का परीक्षण करें: ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट WHO का प्रकाशन है — ग्लोबल फंड एक वित्तपोषण निकाय है, रिपोर्टिंग/डेटा निकाय नहीं। कथन 2 गलत है।
कथन 1 सही + कथन 2 गलत → विकल्प c।
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: ग्लोबल फंड और WHO दोनों टीबी नियंत्रण चर्चा में प्रमुख संस्थान हैं, जो एक ही समाचार चक्रों और आधिकारिक दस्तावेजों में दिखाई देते हैं। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि ग्लोबल फंड टीबी से जुड़ा है, वे टीबी डेटा प्रकाशन को गलती से इसे ही मान सकते हैं, जबकि सही प्रकाशक WHO है। कथन 2 जानबूझकर एक संस्थागत भ्रम है जो देश-स्तरीय टीबी बोझ ट्रैकिंग के बारे में अन्यथा सही लगने वाले वाक्य में निहित है।
solution.final_explanation:
WHO की ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट विश्व स्तर पर टीबी बोझ को ट्रैक करने वाला अधिकारिक वार्षिक प्रकाशन है — जो ग्लोबल फंड से भिन्न है, जो टीबी कार्यक्रमों के क्रियान्वयन को वित्तपोषित करता है।

• कथन 1 — सही: टीबी घटना दर प्रति वर्ष प्रति 100,000 जनसंख्या में नए और पुनरावर्ती मामलों की गिनती करती है; टीबी प्रचलन किसी विशिष्ट समय पर प्रति 100,000 में सभी सक्रिय टीबी मामलों की गिनती करता है। ये अलग-अलग महामारी विज्ञान माप हैं — UPSC ने इस परिभाषात्मक सटीकता को परखा है।
• कथन 2 — गलत: एड्स, टीबी और मलेरिया से लड़ने के लिए ग्लोबल फंड एक बहुपक्षीय वित्तपोषण तंत्र है — यह महामारी विज्ञान डेटा या ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित नहीं करता। WHO वार्षिक ग्लोबल टीबी रिपोर्ट प्रकाशित करता है।

कथन 1 सही + कथन 2 गलत → विकल्प c।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• भारत विश्व के लगभग 26% टीबी घटना का हिस्सा है — सबसे बड़ा राष्ट्रीय हिस्सा।
• टीबी मृत्यु दर प्रति 100,000 जनसंख्या में टीबी से होने वाली मौतों को दर्शाती है — एक तीसरा अलग माप।
• भारत का 'टीबी-मुक्त भारत' 2025 का लक्ष्य घटना दर को प्रति मिलियन 1 से नीचे लाने पर आधारित है — एक सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य उन्मूलन सीमा।

solution.concept_anchor: GDI vs GII vs GGGI — three distinct gender indices, three distinct publishers
solution.strong_distractor: b — Option b incorrectly maps GII to WEF (instead of UNDP), which is the most common confusion since students associate WEF with gender gap reporting.
elimination_logic: Anchor: HDI (A) → UNDP/Human Development Report (2). Unambiguous anchor match.
Verify: GDI (B) → UNDP/HDR (4). GDI is the ratio of female to male HDI — published in the same HDR as GDI. B→4.
Verify: GII (C) → UNDP/HDR (1). Gender Inequality Index measures reproductive health, empowerment, labour market — an HDR product. C→1.
Verify: GGGI (D) → WEF (3). Global Gender Gap Index is a WEF product measuring parity across four sub-indices. D→3.
Full correct match: A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3 → option d.
solution.upsc_trap_explanation: This question places three gender-related indices (GDI, GII, GGGI) in the same question. GDI and GII are both UNDP products from the same HDR, while GGGI is WEF. The trap is attributing GII to WEF (option b) — students who know 'GGGI is WEF' sometimes extend this to GII because both have 'gender' and 'inequality' in their titles. The correct mapping requires distinguishing between: (i) UNDP publishes both GDI and GII through HDR; (ii) WEF publishes GGGI separately.
solution.final_explanation:
Three gender-related indices — GDI, GII, and GGGI — appear frequently in UPSC Prelims, and publisher confusion is the standard trap.

• A (HDI) → 2 (UNDP — Human Development Report): HDI is UNDP's flagship composite index published annually in the HDR.
• B (GDI) → 4 (UNDP — ratio of female to male HDI): GDI computes the ratio of female HDI to male HDI. A value below 1 indicates women have lower HDI than men. Published in the same HDR as GDI.
• C (GII) → 1 (UNDP — reproductive health, empowerment, labour): GII measures gender inequality across three dimensions. It is an HDR product — same publisher (UNDP) as GDI and HDI.
• D (GGGI) → 3 (WEF — gender parity across four sub-indices): GGGI is WEF's index measuring the gap between male and female outcomes in economic participation, education, health, and political empowerment.
